sources.entry: Shutterbar - ShareX-style screenshots with ⌘C-to-clipboard, after-capture tasks, last-region recapture and scrolling capture. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/mucahitimre/Shutterbar) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Shutterbar is a macOS screenshot app inspired by ShareX that copies a selected region to the clipboard with ⌘C, runs configurable after-capture tasks, and recaptures the last region with a shortcut.
summary.what_it_does: Shutterbar lets you select a screen region, a window, or a whole screen and capture it with a frozen-screen overlay so menus and hover states stay put. Pressing ⌘C copies the selection to the clipboard only, while Enter runs a chosen pipeline of tasks: annotate, save to file, copy, show in Finder, and notify, with each failure isolated. The last selected region is remembered across relaunches, and ⌥⇧5 recaptures it without opening the overlay. Scrolling capture stitches frames of long content into one image, either automatically (GitHub build, with Accessibility permission) or manually. The built-in annotation editor offers arrows, rectangles, text, pixelation and numbered steps with undo/redo. The README states that everything stays local with no account or cloud.
use_cases: capture a region and paste it into chat or email
take a long scrolling screenshot of a web page
save and annotate screenshots for bug reports
repeat a before/after screenshot of the same area
replace ShareX-style workflows on a Mac
capture a window with its shadow-free bounds
quickly annotate a screenshot with arrows and text
how_to_run: Or download Shutterbar-x.y.z.dmg from GitHub Releases and drag it to Applications
Build from source: brew install xcodegen
cp Config/Local.xcconfig.example Config/Local.xcconfig (set your Team ID and bundle id prefix)
notable: ⌘C copies a selection straight to the clipboard with no file or dialog
Frozen-screen overlay captures all displays before selection, so menus and tooltips stay visible
Last region is remembered across relaunches and can be recaptured via ⌥⇧5 without the overlay
Scrolling capture with optional automatic scrolling that never moves the pointer and stops at the end of content
Two builds: a GitHub build (non-sandboxed, Developer ID, notarized) and a planned sandboxed App Store build with manual scrolling only
caveats: Requires macOS 14.0 or later and Screen Recording permission
Automatic scrolling needs Accessibility permission and is only in the GitHub (non-sandboxed) build; App Store build is still on the roadmap
No selection spanning multiple screens; selection is clamped to the starting screen
Drawn annotations cannot be individually selected, moved or deleted; use undo
